content_html:
Makeup stains can contain oils, waxes, pigments, or a combination of all three. Lifting the excess without rubbing and treating according to the product base works better than sending the garment straight through a hot dryer.

Lift excess makeup without spreading pigment

Use a dull spoon or card edge to lift thick foundation, lipstick, or dried mascara. Do not scrub outward because pigment can spread into a larger area of fabric.

Treat the oily component first

For makeup containing oils or waxes, a small amount of garment-safe liquid detergent helps emulsify the grease. Work from the back of the stain when practical and follow the fabric care label.

Rinse and repeat before applying heat

Check the stain in good light after rinsing. If pigment remains, repeat a compatible treatment; dryer or iron heat can set residue and make it much harder to remove.

Delicate garments need fabric-specific treatment

Silk, wool, acetate, and dry-clean-only garments can react poorly to detergent or rubbing. If the care label limits washing, take the garment to a professional and identify the type of makeup that caused the stain.
